I would encourage more founders to copy the ideas out there that you’re passionate about. Not because that is your end game, but to the degree it is something you enjoy building, you can get some customers and cockroach. That will give you time to adapt and figure out what unique thing it can evolve to as technology progresses.

In the age of AI, people can build very quickly. So, in many situations, it’s best to be in market with a team, funding, and some customers to take advantage of new capabilities in the models as they come out. It’s much harder to do what we used to do: quietly build a thing for 3-6 months and launch it. By the time you get the company started, you’ll have moved too slowly.

You should assume you will look no different than everyone adjacent to you in the first 3-4 months. However it may only be  like that for 3-4 months.

Something I told 14 yo: The most powerful kind of imagination is the kind that comes from seeing the shapes of ideas. For example, that two ideas fit together like jigsaw puzzle pieces, or that if you change one in some way it has exactly the same shape as another.

Ask Astra (medium) to replicate it to the best of its ability and giving it whatever extra instructions and adaptations you want. Set a /goal like provide proof of the results so it has something to compare to.

After the first run, switch to Astra (max) and give it instructions to polish. And you can keep doing this iteratively to keep improving results.

So there is one component to build and one to optimize/tune.

I think it works well because it breaks the problem down and allows the models to focus efforts as opposed to trying to use lots of tokens for many things at once (usually lower quality results).

This can essentially be done in one go using subagents and /goal.
